Fellow neocloud play Nebius tumbled after lifting its 2026 forecast for capital expenditures spending. Justin Sullivan | Getty Images Austin, Texas-based Yeti Holdings sank 8%, extending a three-day decline, after third-quarter adjusted revenue of $517.9 million missed Wall Street analyst estimates of $523 million and the cooler and travel mug maker lowered full-year forecasts for earnings per share excluding one-time items, adjusted revenue and adjusted operating income. Yeti has now tumbled 14% in three days and more than 22% in the past three months. — Scott Schnipper 2 Hours Ago CoreWeave slides the day after huge post-earnings advance The New Jersey-based neocloud provider sank almost 8%, one day after soaring 25% in the wake of better-than-expected third-quarter results. Fellow neocloud Nebius Group slumped almost 18% after trimming its full-year revenue guidance. CoreWeave has been almost cut in half over the past three months. CoreWeave is off 48% in three months — Scott Schnipper 2 Hours Ago Take-Two slips as BofA flags $1.9 billion opening-weekend bar for GTA VI Chris Delmas | AFP | Getty Images Shares of Take-Two Interactive fell 2% Thursday after Bank of America said Grand Theft Auto VI would need to generate $1.9 billion in sales in its first weekend after launch to "satisfy expectations." TTWO- YTD In the past, GTA 5 had surpassed $1 billion in sales (gross of platform/channel fees) within its first three days. "Although we've maintained that GTA online monetization underpins our bullish view on the stock, investors on both sides of the debate will handicap the franchise's success based on sales figures released shortly after launch," the bank said. — Deena Zaidi 2 Hours Ago Keurig Dr Pepper dips on announcement of $2 billion stock offering The company behind Canada Dry and Snapple slid almost 5% after announcing a proposed $2 billion common stock offering. Nebius- YTD The AI cloud company's net loss narrowed to $37.5 million, or 13 cents per share, from $119.6 million, or 50 cents per share, a year earlier. Revenue surged 571% to $980.8 million, topping the $907.5 million expected by analysts surveyed by LSEG . Nebius is calling for 2026 capex to come in at $27 billion, higher than its earlier forecast for $20 billion to $25 billion. The company also sees 2026 revenue at the low end of its $3 billion to $3.4 billion range, while the FactSet consensus estimate was $3.35 billion. The results follow better-than-expected reports from fellow AI cloud providers CoreWeave and IREN over the past week. Nebius faces political uncertainty after voters backed restrictions on data center development last week. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 's departure from the chip giant also adds to the volatility since Nvidia held about $329 million in Nebius shares at the end of June, according to a filing . — Deena Zaidi 2 Hours Ago SpaceX jumps after announcing new supercompute campus Elon Musk's rocket-building company saw shares rise 2% after announcing the construction of a $50 billion supercompute campus in Cochise County, Arizona. SpaceX also announced it will invest more than $24 billion in new supercomputing infrastructure at its Starbase in Rio Grande Valley, Texas. SpaceX on Thursday Further, CLSA lifted its target price to $300, calling for nearly 115% upside from Wednesday's close. "The hysteria surrounding the US midterms elections and outcomes has largely subsided … for now," wrote analyst Max Hopkins. It forecasts revenue of $2.019 billion to $2.038 billion, while its prior outlook was for $2.037 billion to $2.076 billion. "We see a runway for shares to work from here, with Instinct share gains offering additional upside as AMD stays focused on execution while its largest competitor, Nvidia, contends with a growing leadership and regulatory imbroglio," Sebastien Naji wrote in a Thursday note. Intel is struggling with delays and supply shortages for its next-generation Xeon processor. At Nvidia, the potential departure of CEO Jensen Huang who's embroiled in extramarital scandal could benefit AMD over a multi-year period. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images The cash-strapped United States Postal Service said on Thursday it is seeking ​approval for an 11% price hike for domestic priority mail and ‌package deliveries in January to deal with rising fuel costs. USPS, which needs approval from the Postal Regulatory Commission for the price increase, said it was not planning to hike the price of first-class stamps in January, which rose in July from 78 to 82 cents. The surcharge is rising from a temporary 8% surcharge that was imposed in April. USPS said this week its transportation expenses in the 12 months ending September 30 rose by $225 million due to higher fuel costs. USPS said it was proposing to hike overall domestic shipping services prices 5.9% on average and is raising prices by an average of 7.9% for international deliveries. USPS asked Congress on Tuesday for $2 billion in support and reimbursements as its head warned ​the agency would be forced to make significant cuts in retail post ‌offices and other reductions unless lawmakers act. USPS reported an annual $6.5 billion loss versus a net loss of $9 billion in the prior 12 months. The ​new Democratic-led Congress, which takes office in January, will need to decide whether ​to help the Postal Service after Republicans held a series of hearings ⁠over the last two years on its finances. USPS wants $2 billion from Congress for ​unfunded requirements it has imposed. The agency has recorded net losses of more than $120 billion since ​2007. The volume of first-class mail, its most profitable product, fell this year to its lowest level since 1965 as consumers have moved to digital communication, while USPS must still pay for costly ​nationwide delivery. Postmaster General David Steiner says the ⁠agency has a broken business model and needs help from lawmakers to turn around its operations. In May, ⁠USPS ​suspended non-essential spending on travel, office supplies and consultants. ​USPS also earlier this year temporarily suspended employer payments for a federal pension program. headlines.article_text: Nebius Q3 earnings report 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Nebius results surpassed consensus, but full-year guidance was light. The report comes after fellow neoclouds IREN and CoreWeave showed better-than-expected results in the past week. The companies' stocks have bounced back this week after a brutal past month that reflected concerns about a slowdown in the AI buildout. Nvidia, which invests across the neocloud space, is creating added volatility due to the crisis surrounding CEO Jensen Huang. In this article NBIS Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Arkady Volozh, CEO of Nebius and then Yandex CEO, speaks at the Artificial Intelligence Journey event in Moscow on Nov. 9, 2019. Mikhail Svetlov | Getty Images Nebius shares sank 16% on Thursday as one of the biggest publicly traded neoclouds issued disappointing full-year revenue guidance. Here's how the company performed relative to LSEG consensus: Earnings per share: 31 cents adjusted vs. loss of 69 cents per share expected Revenue: $980.8 million vs. $907.5 million expected Revenue jumped 571% in the quarter, according to a statement . The company reported a net loss of $37.5 million, a loss of 13 cents per share, compared with $119.6 million, a loss of 50 cents per share, a year earlier. The stock move also comes amid the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , after stinging revelations about multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Nvidia, which has developed the neocloud market by investing in the companies and backstopping some of their projects, held about $329 million in Nebius shares at the end of June, according to a filing . In a letter to shareholders , CEO Arkady Volozh said the company expects fiscal year 2026 revenue at the low end of the company's $3 billion to $3.4 billion range. Analysts surveyed by LSEG had $3.37 billion. Nebius also shared an initial outlook for 2027, expecting revenue of $12 billion to $13 billion, "reflecting a conservative approach to the pace of our buildout." The LSEG consensus was $11.98 billion. The company expects FY2026 capital expenditures of $27 billion, higher than its previous capex guidance of $20 billion to $25 billion and the FactSet expectation of $23.85 billion. Nebius' expected FY2027 capex of $40 billion to $45 billion came in much higher than the FactSet expectation of $28.77 billion. Nebius stock chart. Nebius' results come after fellow neoclouds CoreWeave and IREN reported better-than-expected financials in their earnings announcements over the past week. That's provided a boost to the companies' stocks, which had suffered steep selloffs in recent weeks on concern about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence buildout. The neocloud companies posted a robust rally on Wednesday, with Coreweave booming nearly 25%, Nebius climbing 15%, Applied Digital rising more than 7% and IREN adding nearly 6%. Each of the stocks fell Thursday premarket after the Nebius Q3 report. Last week, CoreWeave's bond yields spiked past the 16% mark. In its earnings report on Tuesday, CoreWeave told analysts it expects to keep parent-level debt financing under $5 billion through 2027. During the quarter, Nebius said it raised $5.75 billion in debt financing. "Capital markets have been unsettled lately," CEO Arkady Volozh said on a conference call with analysts. "Two questions are being asked our whole industry, how fast can AI build-out happen, and who will pay for it? These are important questions. The way I think about it is simple. The demand for AI is real and substantial. Everything else, like building the capacity and financing it, is just a task. Tasks can be hard, but they all can be solved." The political backdrop has created further volatility as Nebius races rivals to open up new data centers. Last week U.S. voters supported dozens of ballot initiatives to restrict the development of such facilities, while Democrats won sweeping victories in both houses of Congress.
